newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown orders public spending review.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown orders public spending review.

text.p: Labour's new finance minister Gordon Brown has ordered a fundamental review of public spending and plans the most radical welfare budget of the past 50 years in Britain.
Interviewed by The Observer newspaper, he said: 'I am not interested in measures that just alleviate the problem of youth and long-term unemployment for a few months.
'I'm interested in developing a welfare state built around the work ethic.'
Brown, who won praise from financial markets for giving the Bank of England independence to set interest rates, also promised immediate changes to capital gains tax and corporation tax.
This would encourage more long-term ownership and higher investment.
Amid media speculation that the budget could be introduced as early as June 10, Brown said he had instructed treasury officials to start a public spending review.
This would be completed in time to let him implement a three-year plan for spending from 1998 that would allow increases in priority areas.

In the Observer interview, Brown also promised a bill that would release over time five billion pounds of capital receipts from state council house sales to kick-start a huge social housing programme.
Brown has already promised to bring in a windfall tax on privatised utility companies that would be used to get the long-term jobless and young into work.
